outcomeNote: Mishna rulings with one tannaitic dispute.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נוֹתְנִין קֶמַח לְתוֹךְ חֲרוֹסֶת אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַחַרְדָּל. וְאִם נָתַן — יֵאָכֵל מִיָּד, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹסֵר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One» may «not add flour to ḥaroset,» a seasoned, pungent food, «or to mustard,» to dull the sharp taste. In both cases, the pungency of these foods might accelerate the leavening of the flour. «And if one added» flour to either of these, the mixture may «be eaten immediately» before it is leavened; «and Rabbi Meir prohibits» this, lest the food be leavened immediately.

segments.he: אֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח לֹא בְּמַשְׁקִין וְלֹא בְּמֵי פֵירוֹת, אֲבָל סָכִין וּמַטְבִּילִין אוֹתוֹ בָּהֶן.
segments.en: The mishna continues: «One» may «not boil the Paschal» lamb «in» ordinary «liquids or in fruit juices,» as the Torah explicitly states that it must be roasted. «However,» one may «baste» it while it is roasting «and dip it into» liquid while eating it.

segments.he: מֵי תַשְׁמִישׁוֹ שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹם — יִשָּׁפְכוּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מַחְמִיצִין.
segments.en: The tanna further states: «Water that has been used by a baker» for cooling his hands or washing dishes should «be poured out, because» this water «leavens» the dough, as the water probably contains a small quantity of flour and dough.
